source: NCERT Class XI, Indian Constitution at Work, Ch. 8 (Local Governments).

sections.heading: 1. Why Local Government?
points: **Local government** = government at the village and district/town level — the level closest to ordinary people.
It strengthens **democracy at the grassroots**, allows local problems to be solved locally, and increases people's participation.
Local self-government has old roots in India (village panchayats); reformers like **Gandhiji** stressed village swaraj.

sections.heading: 2. Growth and Constitutional Status
points: After Independence, panchayats were weak (in the Directive Principles only).
The **73rd Amendment (1992)** gave constitutional status to **rural local government (Panchayati Raj)**; the **74th Amendment (1992)** to **urban local government (Municipalities)**.
These came into effect in **1993**.

sections.heading: 3. Key Features of the 73rd/74th Amendments
points: **Three-tier structure** (rural): **Gram Panchayat (village) → Panchayat Samiti/Mandal (block) → Zilla Parishad (district)**.
**Gram Sabha** = the assembly of all voters of a village.
**Regular elections** every 5 years, conducted by the **State Election Commission**.
**Reservation** of seats for **SCs, STs (in proportion) and one-third (now often half) for women**; reservation for OBCs by states.
A **State Finance Commission** reviews the finances of local bodies every 5 years.
The **Eleventh Schedule** (rural, 29 subjects) and **Twelfth Schedule** (urban, 18 subjects) list local functions.

sections.heading: 4. Significance and Limitations
points: Deepened democracy, empowered **women and marginalised groups** (huge number of elected women/SC/ST representatives).
Limitations: **inadequate funds and powers**, dependence on states, dominance of local elites, and bureaucratic control.
Still, local governments are a major democratic experiment.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: 73rd Amendment = rural (Panchayati Raj); 74th = urban (Municipalities); both 1992, effective 1993.
Three-tier: Gram Panchayat → Panchayat Samiti → Zilla Parishad.
Gram Sabha = all voters of a village; elections every 5 years (State Election Commission).
One-third seats reserved for women (now half in many states).
11th Schedule (29 rural subjects), 12th Schedule (18 urban subjects).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **73rd = Panchayats (rural); 74th = Municipalities (urban)** — do not swap.
The **11th Schedule** lists **rural** subjects; the **12th Schedule** lists **urban** ones.
**Gram Sabha = all voters** of a village (not the elected council).
Local body elections are conducted by the **State Election Commission** (not the ECI).
